_doc: Bank salary-transfer offer pages and their T&C documents, watched weekly by the 'salary-transfer' monitor (scripts/monitor/setup.mjs). Like offers, this is a per-BANK surface rather than per-card, which is why it lives here and not on scripts/scrape/banks/<slug>.urls.json. Entries here are alert-only and are never auto-scraped: the salaryTransferOffers collection is entirely typed editor content (salary bands, reward amounts, clawback terms) with no free-text scraper equivalent at all, so a change routes to the business-realestate editor and the deals desk to be typed up against the source. Cadence is weekly rather than daily because salary-transfer promotions move on quarterly campaign cycles; see the credit budget in CLAUDE.md.
_admission_standard: A URL enters `banks` only on evidence, never on plausibility. Either (a) two independent signals — an editor verified it as a live entry's sourceUrl AND discovery independently re-surfaced it — or (b) scripts/monitor/verify-candidates.ts fetched it and returned SUPPORTED. Plausibility is not enough: salaryTransferOfferHistory records that adcb.com/en/personal/promotions/salary-transfer and rakbank.ae/personal/accounts/salary-transfer both returned 404 on re-verification (30 June 2026) despite reading like perfectly ordinary salary-transfer URLs. Candidates that fail stay in _pending with their verdict recorded.

banks._evidence: Owner-supplied 5 August 2026; both fetched same day at HTTP 200. Landing page carries AED amounts, a minimum salary of AED 5,000, a band table and a validity date to 31 December 2026 — SUPPORTED on the verify criteria without a separate run. T&C PDF is the authoritative source and says so explicitly (§6: 'These Terms & Conditions take precedence over any marketing or promotional communication'), so every typed figure in the offer entry derives from it rather than the landing page. Landing page + T&C pair, same shape as the ENBD entry. NOTE: the URL as supplied carried gclid, gbraid and five utm_* parameters; the clean URL was confirmed to resolve on its own and is what is watched here.

Campaign page: live sourceUrl of emirates-nbd-ongoing-2026.mdx, re-surfaced by discovery runs 30982700538 and 30985646889. T&C PDF: verify run 30988856840 returned SUPPORTED (AED 5000, minSalary 5000). Landing page + T&C pair, which is the shape this surface wants. Liv T&C PDF added: SUPPORTED on verify run 31003513821 (5 August 2026) with the strongest signal set of the whole run — AED 5,000, minimum salary AED 5,000, bands AND clawback, all four. Liv is ENBD's digital bank, so this is likely a distinct offer rather than a duplicate of the campaign above; the desk should confirm which product it describes before either is written up.

NEO page: live sourceUrl of mashreq-2026.mdx, re-surfaced by both discovery runs. Gold page: verify run 30988856840 returned SUPPORTED with the strongest signal set of any candidate (AED 50000, minSalary 25000, band language present). NEO salary-transfer-bonus T&C added: SUPPORTED on verify run 31003513821 (5 August 2026) (AED 2,500, bands, clawback). This closes a real gap — mashreq-2026.mdx cites a marketing page as its sourceUrl, and the entry can now be re-derived from the terms document, the same upgrade the FAB entry was built with from the start. Gold-tier T&C added 6 August 2026: the 5 August 502 was transient — re-fetch returned HTTP 200 with all four signal types (band table AED 5,000-9,999 → 200 / 10,000-19,999 → 500 / 20,000-49,999 → 1,000 / 50,000+ → 2,500; minimum salary AED 5,000; 90-day payout; clawback on 2 consecutive missed months within the 6-month cycle). Gold is a distinct tier from NEO with its own bonus table; the desk should treat them as separate offers when writing up.

SWAPPED 6 August 2026 on resolution of the 2026-08-05 source-conflict brief. This is the CURRENT XTRA campaign T&C (its own definitions: start 1 January 2026, min salary AED 5,000, expat bands AED 250-3,000, bundle-gated) and the sourceUrl of the live dib-xtra-2026.mdx entry — full human read on 6 August matched the entry verbatim, satisfying the admission standard on both legs (editor-verified sourceUrl + direct fetch with all signal types). The previously watched 9684-salary-transfer-tc.pdf turned out to be the EXPIRED 10 July - 7 September 2024 campaign (AED 8,000 minimum, smaller bands, prize draw) still hosted; the verify run's SUPPORTED verdict was parsing a real document from a dead campaign. Moved to _pending. Lesson recorded there: deterministic signals confirm a document is a salary-transfer T&C, not that its campaign is alive — campaign dates need a human read.

SUPPORTED on verify run 31003513821 (5 August 2026) — minimum salary AED 5,000, band language and clawback wording, three strong signals. Provenance is notable: this URL came from .council/briefs/2026-05-30-salary-transfer-tracker-unverified-figures.md, which recorded it live on 30 May after adcb.com/en/personal/promotions/salary-transfer returned 404. It sat in an open brief for two months while two discovery runs reported 'no candidate found', because the patterns required 'salary' to start a path segment and this slug carries it as a suffix. Replaces the Mar-2017 PDF, which stays in _pending as WEAK.

Promoted 6 August 2026 on full human read for the rakbank-cash-reward-2026.mdx entry. The cash-reward T&C (July 2026) carries all four signal types: band table AED 500/1,000/2,000/4,000, minimum salary AED 10,000 (5,000 for RAKempower/RAKmore enrollees), three-consecutive-salaries tenure with lowest-month computation, and a clawback clause. Campaign window 1 July - 31 August 2026 — RAKBANK versions these PDFs per campaign cycle (the accounts-lp page lists five dated welcome-interest T&Cs, active and concluded), so when this document's link changes on the RAKmore page, that is the signal a new cycle has started. The RAKmore page itself is the durable landing (min salary AED 5,000, benefits list) and is the entry's secondary source. accounts-lp from the 30 May brief was reviewed and left unwatched: it is a marketing landing that rotates campaign tiles; the RAKmore page + campaign T&C are the load-bearing pair.

Promoted 6 August 2026 after the human look the WEAK verdict asked for. The verdict's hypothesis — bands and clawback in an unreached section — is FALSIFIED: the full T&C is one page and there are no bands, because the ADIB Salary Bonus Programme is a PRIZE DRAW, not a banded offer. Minimum salary AED 3,000, automatic enrollment; 10 monthly winners of 1x salary (capped AED 10,000) and 1 grand winner of 12x salary (capped AED 200,000), prizes at ADIB's discretion, paid from shareholders' funds. A draw has no guaranteed reward, so it cannot honestly occupy salaryBands[] — ADIB stays uncovered in the reader-facing tracker, recorded as a documented finding (same class as Citi's absence, different mechanism). Both URLs watched: if ADIB ever launches a banded cashback offer, one of these surfaces is where it lands.

Hand search 6 August 2026 (per the _no_candidate instruction to locate by hand), HTTP 200. This is the page discovery could never reach: the slug is credit-card-cash-bonus with no 'salary' anywhere in the path, so no pattern variant would ever have ranked it. The page carries a full salary-transfer cash-bonus band table (AED 5,000-14,999 → 1,500; 15,000-24,999 → up to 6,000 bundled; 25,000-49,999 → up to 8,000; 50,000+ → up to 25,000 with card + home loan), minimum salary AED 5,000, three-consecutive-salary-transfers requirement, and one-year clawback — all four signal types. CAVEAT, and it matters: the stated validity is 1 June – 31 August 2024, confirmed by the linked T&C PDF (salary credits due by 31 January 2025). The campaign is OVER; the page is stale-but-published. Watching it is correct — a renewal will move this page — but it is NOT evidence of a live offer and must not seed a reader-facing tracker entry. This settles the backfill brief's open question: CBD did run a salary-transfer offer, through 31 August 2024; whether it currently runs one is answered 'no' as of 6 August 2026.

Hand search 6 August 2026, HTTP 200. Discovery missed it for the same structural reason as CBD: the path /premier/rewards-and-offers/ carries no 'salary'. HSBC's salary-transfer offer lives inside the Premier welcome offer: AED 2,000 cashback for transferring an ongoing monthly net salary of at least AED 40,000 (AED 30,000 for Emirati nationals) within the first 3 months of account opening, sustained for at least 2 consecutive months (footnote 11 on the page). Offer ends 31 December 2026. Three strong signals — AED amount, minimum salary, validity — plus the consecutive-months condition. Note for the desk: this is a high-threshold offer (AED 40,000/month) inside a premium-account package, a different shape from the mass-market band-table offers; the deposit/investment legs of the same welcome offer (AED 8,000-12,000 cashback) are funding-based, not salary-based, and are not what this watch is for. The offer T&C PDF is in _pending — it timed out twice on fetch and its content is unverified.

SUPPORTED on verify run 31003513821 (5 August 2026) — AED 3,000 and band language. CAVEAT, and it matters for coverage: MBRHE is the Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment programme, a narrow eligibility segment for UAE nationals, NOT Emirates Islamic's general salary-transfer offer. Watching it is correct; it does not make Emirates Islamic a covered bank in the reader-facing sense. Its general offers page and both 6k/16k T&C documents came back WEAK on the same run — see _pending.

_pending._doc: Candidates fetched or proposed but not yet meeting the admission standard. Verdicts reflect runs 30988856840, 30990596839 and 31003139057. Not watched. A candidate needs two strong signals — AED amount, minimum salary, band language, clawback wording — on a reachable page that mentions salary transfer. NOTE: URL discovery is not the only source of candidates, and 'no candidate found' has twice meant 'discovery did not reach it'. ADCB's live page sat in an open brief for two months; FAB's was supplied by the owner. Both were invisible because the patterns required 'salary' to start a path segment while both slugs carried it as a suffix — fixed 5 August 2026. Check .council/briefs/ before concluding a bank has no offer.

rakbank.verdict: RESOLVED 6 August 2026 — the May-30 brief's 'up to AED 4,000 cashback' is real and now a live tracker entry (rakbank-cash-reward-2026.mdx); the RAKmore page + campaign T&C moved to `banks`. These three stay unwatched: accounts-lp is a rotating campaign-tile marketing landing, the bare salary-transfer path is a thin index, and the Islamic variant was never verified. The earlier WEAK verdicts were correct about the pages, wrong about the bank — the offer detail lives in the campaign PDF none of the discovery paths surfaced.

standard-chartered.verdict: NO SALARY-TRANSFER CONTENT (unchanged across both runs) — an application form carries little prose. The landing page without /apply is the better watch target and was never proposed by discovery; locate by hand.

adcb.verdict: WEAK (verify run 31003513821 (5 August 2026)) — reachable, AED 12,000, no bands or clawback, and dated March 2017. Superseded for monitoring by the switch-nine page now in `banks`; retained only because a 2017 document may still be the terms behind an older cycle.

emirates-islamic.verdict: ALL WEAK on verify run 31003513821 (5 August 2026), and this reverses what I predicted. I called the 6k/16k T&C documents the most promising candidates in the set; the 6k returned NO signals at all and the 16k only clawback. The general offers page carries AED 6,000 but nothing else. What actually verified was the MBRHE package, which I had dismissed as a narrow segment — now in `banks`. Emirates Islamic's GENERAL offer therefore remains unevidenced, and the bank is not covered in the reader-facing sense. payroll-card retained with its NO SALARY-TRANSFER CONTENT verdict across three runs.

enbd_secondary.verdict: Both WEAK on verify run 31003513821 (5 August 2026). The /en/promotions/ page returned no signals at all despite the promising slug — a reminder that a good URL is not a good page. The abu-dhabi campaign carries AED 15,000 and nothing else, unchanged across two runs.

_no_candidate.note: Hand search completed 6 August 2026 for all three banks previously listed here (cbd, citi, hsbc), per this note's own instruction. CBD and HSBC both had real salary-transfer surfaces that discovery structurally could not reach — neither page carries 'salary' anywhere in its path (cbd: /cbd-rewards/credit-card-cash-bonus; hsbc: /premier/rewards-and-offers/) — both now in `banks` with evidence. Citi is the genuine absence: a 6 August map call returned 47 salary-mentioning URLs on citibank.ae and not one is a transfer offer — they are Salary Protect insurance pages, personal-loan pricing tiers (the fees PDF's 'With Salary Transfer to Citibank 6.99%-8.99%' is loan pricing, not a bonus), and funding-based Citigold promotions (rewards keyed to deposits/investments, not salary). Citi UAE's salary-transfer nexus is loan pricing only; it runs no salary-transfer cashback offer. Recorded as a documented absence, not a discovery failure — the tracker's coverage-gap note can cite this. Prior history of this list, kept because the lesson generalises: FAB and ADCB sat here for months over a one-character anchoring bug (fixed 5 August 2026), and CBD/HSBC sat here because their offer pages carry no 'salary' in the slug at all. Discovery patterns find pages named like offers; they cannot find offers hiding inside differently-named surfaces. Treat any future entry in this list as 'locate by hand', not 'no offer exists'.

cbd.verdict: EXPIRED CAMPAIGN T&C — fetched 6 August 2026 at HTTP 200 during the hand search. Full terms for the 2024 salary-transfer promotion (window 1 June – 31 August 2024, three consecutive salary credits due by 31 January 2025, min AED 5,000, one-year clawback). Content verified but the campaign is over, so it is not watched; the landing page in `banks` is where a renewal would surface. If CBD renews, expect a new T&C document — re-run the hand search then.

hsbc.verdict: UNVERIFIED — fetch timed out twice on 6 August 2026 (60s each, via the MCP channel). This is the T&C PDF behind the Premier welcome offer's salary-transfer leg, linked from the rewards page now in `banks`. Two identical failures means change the channel, not retry: attempt via the Actions verify script on the next run. Until its content is read, the typed figures for any HSBC entry must come from the landing page only, clearly noted as such.

fab.verdict: WEAK (verify run 31003513821 (5 August 2026)) — reachable but AED=0 and no other signal, so the standing account page carries no offer detail of its own. The 20% promotion in `banks` remains the only FAB source worth watching; revisit after it expires 31 December 2026.

dib.verdict: BOTH EXPIRED CAMPAIGNS, resolved 6 August 2026 — DIB leaves dead campaign documents hosted, which is what created the source-conflict brief. The leaflet is the 2018 raffle campaign (valid to 3 September 2018, min AED 8,000). The 9684 T&C is the 10 July - 7 September 2024 XTRA campaign (min AED 8,000, expat bands 350/500/1,000, one-month-salary draw) — the verify run's SUPPORTED verdict on it was real parsing of a dead campaign, which is why campaign dates need a human read on top of deterministic signals. Together they show DIB's minimum was AED 8,000 from at least 2018 through 2024 before the current campaign dropped it to 5,000. Neither is watched; the current dib-xtra-tc.pdf is, in `banks`.
